claim: You can see the Great Wall of China from space.

heard.who: Chinese elementary school textbooks before 2003, as described by Scientific American
heard.quote: The Ministry of Education even moved to revise its elementary school textbooks, which had long claimed the ancient barricade was visible.

answer: Not with the naked eye, in general. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said after his 2003 flight that he had not seen it, and the 2004 photograph from the International Space Station used a zoom lens. Radar satellites can pick the wall out far more easily than a person can.

facts.text: The Great Wall of China is generally not visible to the naked eye from low Earth orbit.

sources.title: Is China's Great Wall Visible from Space?
sources.quote: The unglamorous truth is that the wall is only visible from low orbit under a specific set of weather and lighting conditions.

sources.title: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space?
sources.quote: So while the Great Wall of China can be photographed or observed from space using magnification, it can't be seen with the naked eye.

sources.title: Can You See the Great Wall of China from Space?
sources.quote: "The Great Wall of China is not visible from orbit with the naked eye," Hadfield said via Twitter

facts.text: China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, said after his 2003 flight that he had not seen the Great Wall.

sources.title: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space?

sources.title: Can You See the Great Wall of China from Space?
sources.quote: when China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, went into space in 2003, he said that he couldn't see the structure of the Great Wall from out his capsule window.

facts.text: In 2004 astronaut Leroy Chiao photographed part of Inner Mongolia from the International Space Station with a zoom lens; experts later said the image appears to show the wall, but Chiao himself was not sure.

sources.title: Is China's Great Wall Visible from Space?
sources.quote: NASA experts later confirmed that the photo appears to show the wall. But Chiao admitted that he wasn't sure what he was seeing from space.

sources.title: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space?
sources.quote: on 24 November 2004, an image of the Great Wall of China was captured from low Earth orbit by US astronaut and International Space Station Commander Leroy Chiao.

sources.title: Can You See the Great Wall of China from Space?
sources.quote: took what is thought to be the first verifiable image of the Great Wall of China from out his window on the International Space Station in 2004, using a zoom lens.

contested.text: Whether anyone has seen the wall with the naked eye from low orbit. Scientific American reports that astronauts Eugene Cernan and Ed Lu have said they did; Jeffrey Hoffman says he never saw it.

sources.title: Is China's Great Wall Visible from Space?
sources.quote: Some U.S. astronauts, notably Eugene Cernan and Ed Lu, have said they've seen the wall from low orbit.

sources.title: Is China's Great Wall Visible from Space?
